'''Frances Hellman''' is an American physicist who was dean of the division of mathematical and physical sciences at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 2015 until 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.berkeley.edu/2014/06/11/frances-hellman-to-head-ls-division-of-mathematical-and-physical-sciences/|title=Frances Hellman to head L&S Division of Mathematical and Physical Sciences|publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]]|date=June 11, 2014|access-date=2022-03-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Announcement: Dean of the Division of Mathematical & Physical Sciences {{!}} Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost |url=https://evcp.berkeley.edu/announcement-dean-division-mathematical-physical-sciences |access-date=2022-10-20 |website=evcp.berkeley.edu}}</ref> Her primary academic focus has been the study of the [[thermodynamics|thermodynamic]] properties of novel solid materials, especially [[thin film]] [[semiconductor|semiconducting]], [[superconductivity|superconducting]], and magnetic materials. She has served as chair of the physics department and holds a dual appointment in the materials science and engineering department.

==Early life and education==
Hellman was raised in [[New York City]], where she attended the [[Brearley School]]. She graduated summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa with high honors in physics from [[Dartmouth College]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/frances-hellman|title=Frances Hellman|website=[[University of California, Berkeley]], Physics|access-date=2022-03-14}}</ref> Hellman obtained her [[Ph.D.]] in [[applied physics]] at [[Stanford University]] in 1985.

==Career==
After receiving her Ph.D., Hellman then served as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Bell Laboratories]] from 1985 to 1987, focusing on thin-film magnetism.  She moved to San Diego, California, to become an assistant professor of physics at the [[University of California, San Diego]] 1987, where she worked until 2004. She received tenure in 1994 and became a full professor in 2000.  Hellman is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) and received their [[Joseph F. Keithley Award|Joseph F. Keithley Award For Advances in Measurement Science]] in 2006.

Hellman joined [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]]'s Physics Department in January 2005. She served as chair of the department from 2007 to 2013. In 2019, she was elected to be the 2020 vice president of the American Physical Society and in 2022 became the president of APS.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Presidents |url=http://www.aps.org/about/governance/presidents.cfm |access-date=2022-10-20 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal==

Hellman is the daughter of Chris and [[Warren Hellman]] of [[San Francisco]]. The Hellman family is involved philanthropically with a variety of causes, including the University of California.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sandiegoreader.com/news/2000/feb/24/ucsd-big-money-and-ball-club/|title=UCSD's Robert Dynes, Frances Hellman, and the San Diego Padres|publisher=[[San Diego Reader]]|date=February 24, 2000|access-date=2022-03-14}}</ref>
Frances Hellman married [[Robert Dynes]], former UC President, in May 1998 and they divorced in 2006. In 2006, she met Warren Breslau and married him in 2009.
